name: Cinder
tagline: A scorched world under a crater-pocked sky.

objectives.text: Gravity gets weaker with distance, and stronger with more mass.
An orbit is falling around a world while moving sideways fast enough to keep missing it.
Flying past a moving moon or planet can add speed for free (a gravity assist).
In undisturbed rock layers, deeper layers are older.

name: Veil
tagline: Yellow clouds hide a surface hotter than an oven.

objectives.text: Gases like carbon dioxide trap heat; too much makes a world far hotter.
objectives.chapter: CBSE Class 8 Science: Pollution of Air and Water

objectives.text: Liquid water needs a world at the right distance from its star: the habitable zone.
Air pushes back on fast-moving objects; spacecraft can use it to slow down.
The most fuel-efficient way between two orbits uses two well-timed burns.

name: Hollow
tagline: A world scoured by its own star's light.

objectives.text: Light takes time to travel, so we see distant stars as they were in the past.
objectives.chapter: CBSE Class 8 Science: Stars and the Solar System

objectives.text: Stars change over their lives; a Sun-like star slowly brightens, then swells into a red giant.
There are balance points where a small object can ride along with a planet.
To leave a world for good you need enough speed: escape velocity.

name: Tides
tagline: A moon being slowly pulled apart.
teaser: Something tore a moon into rings. Tidal forces, the Roche limit, and a world that always shows one face.

objectives.text: Tidal forces stretch moons and can lock their spin.

name: Ice
tagline: An ocean hidden under a frozen shell.
teaser: The Orrin tried to move outward, to where water stays liquid under ice.

objectives.text: Beyond the ice line, water freezes; some moons hide liquid oceans below.

name: Spore
tagline: Life that refused to give up.
teaser: Tough microbes adapted as their star brightened. What are the signs of life from far away?

objectives.text: Some gases in an atmosphere can hint at life.

name: Glass
tagline: Air stripped away by a stellar wind.
teaser: Without a magnetic shield, a star's wind can blow a world's air into space.

objectives.text: A magnetic field can shield an atmosphere from the stellar wind.

name: Origin
teaser: The final message, a red giant's glow, and what the Orrin wanted us to know.

objectives.text: Sun-like stars end as red giants, planetary nebulae and white dwarfs.
